title: Petal Springs triage ops scratchbook
content:
Meeting: Petal Springs (community clinic) kickoff — 2025-10-09
Attendees: Dr. Hannah Lee (CTO-equivalent), Rajiv (IT), Daniela Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya N. (Redwood AE)

Purpose: Capture requirements and immediate blockers for a minimally invasive VPC/private deployment of triage assistant (symptom intake -> suggested next steps). They want to run on-prem adjacent (customer-managed VPC) with strict PHI controls. This is a working scratchbook — loose thoughts, gotchas, action items.

High-level customer goals:
- Replace phone intake for after-hours triage with chat-first intake to reduce RN screening time by ~30%
- Keep all PHI inside their VPC; Redwood control plane allowed but metadata audit logs preferred to be pushed to customer's SIEM
- Support 2 concurrent clinician workflows (peak concurrency estimate: 10 concurrent sessions across site)
- Short ramp: pilot in 6 weeks if no major infra/legal blockers

Hard requirements (non-negotiable):
1) No raw patient messages stored outside customer VPC. Any telemetry sent to Redwood control plane must be scrubbed/hashed and only include non-PHI metrics.
2) KMS integration for model keys / secrets (they use AWS KMS in account 111222333).
3) FIPS endpoints required for audit logs ingestion (they flagged compliance team).
4) EHR connectivity: one-way event write into Epic via HL7/REST — we need exact HL7 spec from Rajiv.

Performance constraints / SLOs they care about:
- Target p95 latency for single-turn generation: < 350ms for clinician-facing summary generation (after prompt prep).
- Token budget: want to cap per-session tokens to control cost; suggested 1.5k input + 1k output as initial cap.
- Availability: pilot tolerates 99.5% (non-critical), production will want 99.9% SLA.

Prelim infra notes / options we discussed:
- Private (VPC) deployment: customer's VPC peered to Redwood private runtime; control plane in Redwood but can be configured to not persist PHI.
- On-prem appliance: more friction, but possible for full air-gap (they would consider later if VPC not approved).
- Model choice: start with a small open LlamaX v2 variant (-client validated) tuned to health prompts. We suggested Redwood-verified quantized variant to reduce memory.

Integration gotchas called out during call (capture verbatim-ish):
- "We cannot expose patient IDs even as hashed values to external systems without legal sign-off." -> implies we must add a field-level redaction step before any metrics flow out.
- "Our SSO is SAML + Okta; we need RBAC mapping for clinician roles (RN vs MD)." -> Rx: map SAML groups to Redwood API tokens/scopes.
- Network: outbound-only egress from their subnet is heavily firewalled; they requested a static IP range for Redwood egress endpoints.
- Epic hooks: their HL7 endpoint rejects blank fields; Redwood middleware must ensure required stubs are present.

Data and privacy phase plan (sketch):
Phase 0 - Discovery (this): collect HL7 spec, security questionnaire, list of PII patterns they consider sensitive, and an initial architecture diagram.
Phase 1 - Pilot (limited to 3 clinics): VPC-based private runtime, model pinned to quantized variant, logging disabled for PHI, minimal telemetry (latency counts).
Phase 2 - Expand: add KMS-managed keys for model encryption, SIEM forwarding, optional on-prem appliance evaluation.

Open questions for customer / internal follow-ups:
- Rajiv to share Epic HL7 schema and test sandbox endpoint (deadline: 2025-10-16).
- Legal to confirm allowed telemetry fields and hashing requirements (internal RJ ticket raised).
- Compliance: confirm whether FIPS-only endpoints are mandatory or preferred.
- Exact concurrency estimate and expected user journey (RN handoff frequency) — affects batch sizing and cache TTLs.

Technical considerations / SE notes:
- Suggest enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated clarifying questions to keep token cost down during multi-turn triage. Cache TTL 2 minutes to start.
- Quantized model variant should be tested for hallucination rate on a small prompt set (we need to run ~50 clinical prompts). Add to Redwood Optimize evals.
- Batching: for clinician summary generation, use small batches (batch size 4) with latency SLO to hit p95 < 350ms. Need to test on dedicted pool spec (A100x4 or equivalent).
- Network: request static egress IPs list and port whitelist for their firewall team. Provide a CIDR block and preflight connectivity guide.

Immediate action items (owner + due):
- Rajiv (Petal Springs): send HL7 spec + sandbox URL (due 2025-10-16)
- Daniela (Redwood SE): produce short architecture diagram + proposed VPC peering steps and static IPs (due 2025-10-14)
- Priya (AE): starter contract template and security questionnaire to legal (due 2025-10-15)
- Evan (Redwood infra): provision a disposable test runtime (non-PHI) with quantized LlamaX variant for initial evals (due 2025-10-20)
- Compliance: draft telemetry whitelist + examples of hashed-only metrics to propose (due 2025-10-18)

Quick trial plan (3-week sandbox outline):
Week 0: infra prep + connectivity tests (HL7 sandbox, firewall preflight)
Week 1: deploy private runtime in their VPC, run 50 synthetic symptom prompts, evaluate latency & hallucination
Week 2: integrate HL7 write path, simulate clinician handoffs, finalize RBAC token mapping
Week 3: small pilot with live but consented users (3 clinics), collect telemetry, retrospective and go/no-go decision

Notes to self (SE heuristics / reminders):
- Keep prompt engineering conservative for first pilot (explicit extractive fields + templated summary) to reduce hallucination risk.
- Build a pre-output redaction pass for any PHI tokens (names, MRNs, DOB patterns) before any external logging.
- Add regression evals into Redwood Optimize with baseline of 50 clinical prompts (compare LlamaX quantized vs half-precision).
- Prepare fallback policy: if latency > 600ms or hallucination detected, fall back to a smaller template-only response and flag for manual review.

End of scratchbook entry. Will convert to a formal intake doc once Rajiv sends HL7 and legal confirms telemetry allowances.

-- Daniela R., quick notes saved locally (working).
